text:
The biggest story in St. Louis is in goal. ESPN reported that Joel Hofer has supplanted Jordan Binnington as the starter, and our numbers explain why: Binnington is .844 and 3.9 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, while Hofer has saved 4.9 more than expected over his last five and is .919 against hard shots. For a goalie who won a Stanley Cup here in 2019, it's a hard turn.

The Blues are 13-9-3 with points in five straight, but the process is thinner than the record. They got 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in that run and 48.5% for the season, and our numbers say they have about 3.4 points more than their play deserved. Playoff odds: 41%.

The offense has carried it. Robert Thomas was named the NHL's first star of the week after a ten-point week, and Jake Neighbours tied a franchise record with five assists against New Jersey. Thomas, Dylan Holloway and Jimmy Snuggerud play the most together, and Logan Mailloux has nine points in eight games from the back end. Mason McTavish and Connor McMichael have given the middle six a new look. What we'd watch: whether the Hofer change cuts the goals against enough to make up for a team that still spends more time defending than attacking.
headline: Joel Hofer has taken the Blues' net
